stem.en: A farmer plants two varieties of maize side by side. Seeds form only when pollen from one variety reaches the stigma of the other. What type of pollination is this?

text.en: Self-pollination within one flower of a plant

feedback.en: The pollen here comes from a different variety, so it is not from the same flower.
Yes. Pollen goes from a flower of one plant to a flower of another plant.

text.en: Self-pollination between flowers of one plant

feedback.en: Flowers of one plant are all the same variety. Here two varieties are needed.

text.en: No pollination, since wind carries the pollen

feedback.en: Wind is a pollinator. Pollen reaching a stigma is pollination, whatever carries it.

explanation.en: Pollen from a plant of one variety reaches the stigma of a plant of another variety. Two plants of the same type are involved, so this is cross-pollination.

hints.en: Does the pollen stay on its own plant?
